findings.claim: The registered hooks invoke dist/*.mjs files that are not added by this diff, so a fresh checkout will not be able to run the hooks until an untracked build is performed.
findings.evidence: .claude/settings.json registers `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/dist/agent-ledger.mjs` and `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/hooks/dist/karpathy-flush.mjs`, while the diff adds only `.claude/hooks/src/**/*.mts` and tests importing `../dist/...`; acceptance criterion 5.1 says `check:dist` must pass and the Impact section says new dist files are included.
findings.suggested_fix: Commit the generated `.claude/hooks/dist/**/*.mjs` artifacts and the `scripts/check-dist.mjs`/tsconfig needed to validate them, or change registrations to run a committed executable entrypoint.

findings.claim: The KBD boundary hook registration is not Windows-capable because it relies on POSIX `$PWD` shell expansion.
findings.evidence: The task/change/phase commands are strings like `node "$PWD/.claude/hooks/dist/karpathy-boundary.mjs" --boundary task --project-root "$PWD"`, but acceptance criterion 4 and the spec require KBD boundaries to be recorded on every platform through a Node entry point.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a cross-platform exec/args form supported by the KBD dispatcher, or pass the project root via an environment variable/dispatcher placeholder that works on Windows instead of `$PWD`.

findings.claim: The knowledge-base ingestion timeout is 120 seconds, not the required 10 seconds.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 3.1 requires `pk ingest --scope project --source claude-hooks` with a 10s timeout, but `PK_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` is set to `120_000` and `ingest()` defaults to that timeout.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a 10_000 ms timeout for the `pk ingest` call or update the accepted requirement before shipping this behavior.

findings.claim: The ledger privacy boundary can still commit secrets because identifier sanitization allows credentialed DSNs and email-shaped values into committed JSONL fields.
findings.evidence: `sanitizeId()` accepts `[A-Za-z0-9._:@/+-]+`, which permits values such as `postgres://user:pass@host` and `alice@example.org`; `entryFromHook()` writes sanitized `session_id`, `agent_type`, `agent_id`, and `tool_name` directly to `.prometheus/agent-ledger.jsonl`, while the change rationale says committed `.prometheus/` logs must carry no patient data or secrets by construction.
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten identifier validation to disallow `@`, URL schemes, and credential separators, or run the same PHI/secret scan against ledger lines before appending.
